meta.chapter: The Mounts, Their Position and Their Meanings (Chapter XV)
meta.mount_leaning_track: PARKED behind a vision-measurement gate (S119 Step 5, ratified). Cheiro p113 "THE LEANING OF THE MOUNTS TOWARD ONE ANOTHER" carries real doctrine (e.g. Saturn leaning to Jupiter lends prudence and solemnity to Jupiter's qualities), and it is the only route by which Saturn / Mercury / Lower Mars / Luna could ever produce a discriminating claim. It is NOT built here: no vision signal measures inter-mount lean. Do not author leaning rules until such a measurement exists.
meta.mount_base_meaning_model: S119 Step 5 (ratified): base meanings are DEFINITIONS, not standalone claims. A mount fires only on GRADED doctrine. A base meaning may appear only as consequent context inside a graded rule whose OWN citation contains it (see M_021). Mercury / Lower Mars / Luna base meanings stay in parked_pending (M_P01/M_P02/M_P03, ontology_gap_presence) and Saturn's p112 base meaning is now retired -- those mounts are honestly silent absent grade doctrine or a leaning signal.

Authored as a single-antecedent Saturn-only rule per this task's explicit instruction (a locked content decision), but this is NOT a clean standalone Mounts-chapter doctrine sentence the way M_001-M_014 are. RECOMMEND Sulabh choose one of: (a) keep as-is with this caveat on record, (b) re-scope as a compound rule requiring the Line of Head precondition too, (c) soften the claim wording to something less clinically loaded than 'morbid', or (d) drop/park pending a Line-of-Head-profile signal.

retired_superseded.retired_note: S119 Step 5 (ratified 2026-08-30, Sulabh): mount BASE MEANINGS ARE DEFINITIONS, NOT CLAIMS. This rule hung its mount's ungraded base-meaning sentence on a Development GRADE that the sentence itself never states. Cheiro marks the distinction explicitly and within a single page: p112 writes "When developed" for Jupiter and "When well developed" for Apollo, but plainly "denotes"/"gives" for Venus-base, Saturn and Mercury. A base meaning that holds for the mount as such produces a line true of essentially every hand -- a Barnum statement -- and grading it does not make it discriminating, it only makes the citation disagree with the antecedent. NOTE: the source_quote was and remains verbatim-correct and gate-clean; scripts/gate_rule_citations.py verifies quote AUTHENTICITY and has no notion of antecedent-quote AGREEMENT, which is why this class survived every gate run. Retired, not deleted.

Cheiro marks the distinction explicitly and within a single page: p112 writes "When developed" for Jupiter and "When well developed" for Apollo, but plainly "denotes"/"gives" for Venus-base, Saturn and Mercury. A base meaning that holds for the mount as such produces a line true of essentially every hand -- a Barnum statement -- and grading it does not make it discriminating, it only makes the citation disagree with the antecedent. NOTE: the source_quote was and remains verbatim-correct and gate-clean; scripts/gate_rule_citations.py verifies quote AUTHENTICITY and has no notion of antecedent-quote AGREEMENT, which is why this class survived every gate run. Retired, not deleted.
